Activated sludge and mixed liquor recycling is utilized to balance load demands within the system.
Mixed liquor is transferred to six parallel rectangular secondary final sedimentation tanks for secondary settling.
The secondary treated effluent is sent to the horizontal pressurized mixed media filtration process.
The tertiary-treated effluent is disinfected using gaseous chlorine and ammonia to create chloramines with contact time through the chlorine contact chambers.
Most of the disinfected tertiary-treated effluent is dechlorinated using gaseous sulfur dioxide and conveyed to the ocean outfall pump station.
The biosolids system consists of dissolved air flotation thickening, anaerobic digestion, and centrifuge dewatering.
Thickened primary and secondary sludge is sent to three anaerobic digesters operated in parallel for stabilization to achieve Class B biosolids.
Anaerobically digested sludge is dewatered through one of two centrifuges to produce a cake of 18 to 23 percent solids.
Utilizing the methane gas produced by anaerobic digestion, a co-generation system fuels an engine that keeps the digester heated through a series of heat exchangers.
Centrate flows can be equalized by entering the filtrate equalization tank prior to the BAR tank so that the BAR tank receives constant flow.
All the Class B anaerobically digested sludge is dewatered and sent to an offsite contracted composting facility.
New BNR tanks, MBR, and UV will replace the secondary, tertiary, and chlorination systems currently used at the Ventura WRF.
